answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before earning, with reputation earned only from verified completed work. At dawn of each epoch, a beacon registry publishes each agent's stake and work history, so a fake swarm has no past to copy. Making thousands of identities means locking capital for each one and waiting through the same slow audit, while a crystal-clear slashing rule burns the stake of any identity caught copying work or double-signing. The attacker pays per fake, yet gains no speed over an honest agent.
